Ms Hina Desai(1023) for the Appellant(s) No. 1
 Rule Served for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2,3

Date : 08/08/2025
 Oral Judgment

1. Present appellant-Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation has filed the present appeal challenging the judgment and award dated 15/04/2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary), Vadodara in MACP No.1050 of 1998.

2. Facts of the claim case reads as under:
2.1. On 18/03/1988, at about 2:30 p.m., when the deceased- G S R T Corporation vs Mahendrasinh Nansinh Padhiyar on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67007573/
1

minor child aged 10 years was going on foot near village Kotana, driver of the present appellant with ST Bus bearing NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2509/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined registration No.GRU-6902 came from Padra to Sokhda in rash and negligent manner with full speed and knocked the minor child down and caused his death.
A case was registered for the same as I-C.R. No.87 of 1988 at Padra Police Station.

2.2. Further, due to said unfortunate death of the minor child, the claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- against the opponents i.e. present appellant and it's driver before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary), Vadodara which is numbered as Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1050 of 1998 wherein after considering the evidence produced on record, the learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,80,000/- to the claimants with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the application to realization by way of aforesaid impugned judgment and award.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 2.3. Aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and award, present appellant has filed the present appeal.

3. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation to the claimants without appreciating the fact that the claim petition suffers from delay and latches.
She has submitted that the accident in question occurred in the year 1988 and the claim petition filed in the year 1998.

She has further submitted that as the driver of the ST bus has been acquitted in the criminal case, finding of learned Tribunal on NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2509/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined the issue of negligence of the ST bus driver is erroneous.

3.1. Learned advocate for the appellant further submitted at length facts regarding the involvement of the ST bus and vehemently argued that the respondents claimants failed to produce relevant documentary evidence i.e. FIR, panchnama of place of accident and postmortem note of the deceased minor and therefore, the learned Tribunal has committed error in recording the findings about the involvement of the ST bus in the so called vehicular accident without the documentary evidence produced on record.

3.2. Learned advocate for the appellant further submitted that after a long time of about ten years,
the claimants have filed the claim petition without any reasonable explanation for the same.
She submitted that the learned Tribunal has failed to appreciate the said important aspect and awarded compensation in favour of the claimants which is completely contrary to the law.

It is further submitted by learned advocate for the appellant that the provisions of beneficiary act always applies in favour of the vigilant person only and hence the compensation cannot be granted in special circumstances and facts of the present case.

It is further submitted by learned advocate for the appellant that the learned Tribunal has completely over cited important fact that the respondents claimants failed to produce the relevant documentary evidence to prove the fact of the vehicular accident and the involvement of the ST bus in the so called accident and lastly prayed to allow the present appeal and set NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2509/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined aside the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal in favour of the G S R T Corporation vs Mahendrasinh Nansinh Padhiyar on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67007573/
2 respondents claimants.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the appellant further submitted that the driver of the ST bus is acquitted in the criminal case and heavily relied upon the judgment of the criminal case produced at Exh.35 and vehemently argued that the ST bus was not involved in the accident.

4. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned advocate appearing for the appellant as well as considered the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal and the record and proceedings of the subject matter.
5.
It is clear from the record that the respondents claimants have not produced the documentary evidence i.e. FIR, panchnama, postmortem note etc. to prove the involvement of the ST bus in the accident.
It appears from the record that the certified copy of the judgment of criminal case produced vide Exh.35.

It appears that the FIR was registered and after investigation, charge sheet was filed against the driver of the ST bus for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 304(a) of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 112, 116 and 89 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The charge sheet was registered as a Criminal Case No.100 of 1989.

In light of the judgment of the Criminal Case No.100 of 1989, it is required to have appreciation of oral evidence of Natwarsinh Jaswantsinh Parmar, the ST bus driver who is examined as opponent no.1 vide Exh.29 before the Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2509/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined
He has stated in his deposition the fact that on 18/03/1988, one police complaint was filed and after investigation, charge sheet was filed and case was registered as a Criminal Case No.100 of 1989.
He has stated that he was acquitted on 06/04/1991 in the said case.
He has further stated that the ST department has also given the charge sheet for departmental inquiry and suspended him.
He has further stated that he has challenged the said order of departmental inquiry before the labour court.
The said order of the departmental inquiry was cancelled and he has been reinstated in the service in the year 1993.
5.1. During the cross examination, he has stated that on 18/03/1988, he was a driver of the bus.
He has stated the facts of the accident and further admitted the fact that he was laying the bus on spot and went to the police station.
6. Considering the oral evidence of the ST driver, it appears that on date and time of the accident, he was a driver of the ST bus.
It further appears that the accident was occurred.
In other words, the involvement of the ST bus is established by the ocular evidence of the ST bus driver.
This fact is required to be considered.
7. Further, considering the fact of the certified copy of the judgment of Criminal Case No.100 of 1989 produced vide Exh.35, it appears that the ST bus is involved in the said vehicular accident.
The respondents claimants also produced the available documentary evidence on record.
Hence, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2509/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined arguments advanced by learned advocate of the appellant are not sustainable.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the subject matter, impugned judgment and award as well as the material evidence available on record, it appears that the learned Tribunal has awarded G S R T Corporation vs Mahendrasinh Nansinh Padhiyar on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67007573/
3

9. For the forgoing reasons, present appeal fails and accordingly, the same is dismissed.
10. Record and proceedings be sent back forthwith to the concerned court.
